item.title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail — Sat Nov 14, 1:30 PM — Soulpepper Theatre
item.description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”
This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL
The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.
In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.
Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.
Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

item.title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons — Sat Nov 14, 5:00 PM — The Assembly Theatre
item.description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?
Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.
Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.
The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Participants will receive a WRAP certificate upon program completion. In an 8-week WRAP group, individuals explore: self-care tools like peer connections, relaxation and mindfulness techniques, stress reduction strategies, and more resources for keeping well and feeling better in difficult times. Interested in learning more? Drop in for the information session on Saturday, October 17, 2026, 10 am-12 pm . This WRAP Group meets every Saturday, once a week for 8 weeks, October 24 - December 12, 2026, 10 am-1 pm . Registration closes after week 3, or when full. TTC Presto tickets will be provided. Snacks and refreshments are provided for all participants. Ingredient lists will be available at the program. This program is in collaboration with Gerstein Crisis Centre's WRAP initiative . item.title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America — Tue Nov 24, 7:00 PM — Toronto Reference Library
item.description: TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with Vinh Nguyen at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday. More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist. In his epic new cultural biography Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America , acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon.
